clue.text: Special key to prevent access to room initially

indicators.note: tells us the word for room comes first, ahead of the word for barring

parts.note: room in the sense of empty area means space
to bar a door is to prevent access

explanation.surface: Someone wants a special key to stop people getting into a room at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' attaches to 'room', putting SPACE ahead of BAR though the clue gives the barring first.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar along the bottom of a keyboard is a key with its own particular job.

clue.text: Was fractious, but obeyed Newbolt's captain

definitions.meaning: behaved badly or gave trouble, as a fretful child does
in Henry Newbolt's poem Vitaï Lampada the captain urges 'Play up! play up! and play the game!', so obeying him means doing that

explanation.surface: A team member was difficult but still followed the captain in Newbolt's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Vitaï Lampada is a well-known Victorian English poem about schoolboy cricket and patriotic duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who misbehave are said to act up in this way; the captain's refrain is a famous line.

clue.text: Installing freezer in study, I needed guides

indicators.note: putting the freezer inside the study word makes one piece sit within another
putting the freezer inside the study word makes one piece sit within another

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
an icer is something that freezes or chills
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fits a freezer in their study and needs guides to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of an Italian word for a sightseeing guide; the Latin -i ending is the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: These are guides who show tourists around sights and explain them, named after the orator Cicero.

clue.text: Fuss over who said mild swear-word

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed over another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: bally is a dated British euphemism for bloody

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word who sounds like hoo

parts.note: the pronoun as heard

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss over a person who said a mild swear-word.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLY is a genteel old British stand-in for 'bloody'. 'over' places it on top of the sound of 'who' in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy publicity or commotion; a synonym of fuss and to-do.

clue.text: Where many are annually conducted round building in London

definitions.text: Where many are annually conducted round building in London

parts.words: Where many are annually conducted round building in London
parts.note: reads like a tour route, but the many are orchestras and audiences 'conducted' at the summer Proms in a round concert hall in Kensington

explanation.surface: A guided tour that takes crowds round a London building every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conducted' suggests guides, but means conductors; the venue hosts the annual BBC Proms concerts and is round in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous circular concert venue in South Kensington, home of the Proms each summer.

clue.text: Doctor's work likely to achieve perfection?

definitions.meaning: a doctor's surgery and business, the medical firm a GP runs
the proverb says repetition of an exercise makes perfect

explanation.surface: A doctor's job is likely to be done perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A GP's business is called this, and the saying holds that rehearsal makes perfect.

clue.text: Threatening military alliance in sticky situation

indicators.note: the alliance goes inside the word for a boggy place

parts.note: miry describes muddy, boggy, sticky ground
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance

explanation.surface: A military alliance finds itself in a sticky, threatening situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for menacing, from Latin for threaten.

clue.text: Getting straight to the point? That's a smart quality

parts.note: a drink taken straight is neat, with no mixer
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone praises directness: getting to the point is a smart quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight' is not direct but undiluted; NESS (a headland) appears in British place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness and trimness are the virtue of looking smart and well kept.

clue.text: Make too many demands, showing unconcealed anger

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
ire means wrath or anger

explanation.surface: Someone who demands too much ends up showing open anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone by asking too much effort of them.

clue.text: Base old corps with treaty partner

parts.note: RASC is the Royal Army Service Corps, a former British Army unit
an ally is a nation joined by treaty

explanation.surface: An old army corps sides with a treaty partner in some base scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military base but is the definition, meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of low, roguish and dishonest behaviour.

clue.text: I must enter part of Circle Line platform for transport

indicators.note: the letter goes into the curve's word, entering it

parts.note: an arc is part of the line of a circle
taken as written
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: A traveller on part of London's Circle Line Underground boards from the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here it is just a circle's circumference.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes are a means of travel, so collectively they are a form of transport.

clue.text: Giving away fish caught by bishop and others

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the fish is held inside the Latin phrase, caught by it

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A bishop and others hand out the fish they have caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving away secrets or a friend is treachery, an act of disloyalty.

clue.text: Remedy for the lovesick?

parts.note: split, the word suggests being against doting, which would cure someone besotted

explanation.surface: Someone asks what cures a broken heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure that counteracts poison; split up it reads as opposed to doting.

clue.text: Attractive double feature resulting from book

definitions.meaning: two lovely azure features of a face
a novel by Thomas Hardy, published 1873

explanation.surface: An attractive cinema double bill turns out to be adapted from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double feature' suggests two films, but means a matching set of features on a face; the book is an early Thomas Hardy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two attractive sky-coloured features of a face, and the title of a Hardy novel.

clue.text: Like Hook, or his original character?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Captain Hook in Peter Pan is a pirate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person resembles Captain Hook or his original character.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Hook's first letter, H, which is a breathed sound; 'character' means letter, not personality.
explanation.definitionFit: H is a breathed letter, the kind of sound phoneticians call by this name.

clue.text: Inflammatory material a fool rudely put forward

parts.note: git is a rude British word for a fool
prop is short for propose or proposition, put forward

explanation.surface: Someone rudely calls the person who put forward the inflammatory material a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is a mildly offensive British insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Political propaganda, especially in art or literature, meant to stir people up.

clue.text: On overthrow, one might try to make an escape

definitions.text: On overthrow, one might try to make an escape

parts.words: On overthrow, one might try to make an escape
parts.note: in cricket, when a throw from a fielder goes past the stumps, batsmen dash for extra runs; elsewhere fleeing is the sense

explanation.surface: After a coup, someone tries to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: An overthrow in cricket is a wild return from a fielder that lets batsmen take extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to flee quickly, and also to dash between the wickets.

clue.text: We'd turn out to keep nothing that's current

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the zero within them
out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: We'd turn out to keep nothing that's up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the seven letters into UNDERTW; 'to keep' then holds O. 'current' is a flow of water, not up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: A pull of water beneath the surface, flowing against the waves.

clue.text: Plant British put out for special delight

indicators.note: the letter is ejected from the plant's name

parts.note: euphorbia is a spurge plant

explanation.surface: A British plant is thrown out to everyone's special delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense happiness or elation, a special joy.

clue.text: Regular work on paper over at end of day

parts.note: even means regular or uniform

indicators.note: over signals that the editing word turns back to front

parts.note: to edit is to work on a written text

explanation.surface: Regular paperwork is finished at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Hook holding one Parisienne's black dressing gown

indicators.note: the hook word contains the single unit

parts.note: a peg is a hook to hang things on
I is the Roman numeral one
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A hook holds a Parisian woman's black dressing gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's light loose robe or négligée, a French word.

clue.text: An eruption of small children

parts.note: suggests a swarm of kids, but the eruption is of new teeth through infant gums

explanation.surface: A crowd of little children bursts out.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies cut their first teeth as they break through the gums.

clue.text: Stretch professional received in disgrace

indicators.note: the stretch word takes in the professional

parts.note: reach means stretch or extent
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman takes a long stretch in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of shame, as in being beyond blame or a discredit.

clue.text: Space-traveller repaired radio set

indicators.note: fixed, so the letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A spaceman fixes a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the Sun travels through space.

clue.text: Hot means up-to date? That's about right

indicators.note: the up-to-date word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: topical means current, up to date

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being hot means being current, and is told that's about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid climates near the equator are hot.

clue.text: Time to make the most of the beach

definitions.text: Time to make the most of the beach

parts.words: Time to make the most of the beach
parts.note: sounds like ideal holiday weather, but means when the sea has retreated furthest and most sand shows

explanation.surface: Advice on the best time for a day at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb of the tide, when the shore is most exposed.
